title: Bounded below injective descent and shift-compatible comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal A'$ be abelian categories with enough injectives [def-sp-abelian; def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Write $K^+(\mathcal A)$ for the homotopy category of bounded below integer cochain complexes, $D^+(\mathcal A)$ for its localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category; def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], and $K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\mathcal A)$ for the full subcategory on complexes with injective terms. Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category and let $F:K^+(\mathcal A)\to K^+(\mathcal B)$ and $F':K^+(\mathcal A')\to K^+(\mathcal B)$ be exact functors, equipped with their shift comparisons [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $E:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ be additive and exact, and also write $E$ for its termwise functor and $D^+E$ for the induced derived functor. Suppose $\tau:F\Rightarrow F'E$ is a natural transformation on homotopy categories compatible with the shift comparisons.
There are exact functors $RF:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ and $RF':D^+(\mathcal A')\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ computed by applying $F,F'$ to bounded below injective representatives. For $K$, choose quasi-isomorphisms $k:K\to I$ and $k':EK\to J$ to bounded below complexes of injectives. Choose a chain map $u:EI\to J$ such that $u\circ E(k)$ and $k'$ are homotopic. The morphism represented by
$$F(I)\xrightarrow{\tau_I}F'(EI)\xrightarrow{F'(u)}F'(J)$$
defines a natural transformation $R\tau:RF\Rightarrow RF'\circ D^+E$, independent of $I,J,k,k',u$ under the canonical comparison isomorphisms. It is natural for every morphism in $D^+(\mathcal A)$, including morphisms $K\to L[1]$, and commutes with the induced shift comparisons. The construction respects identity and composition of such comparison data. No assumption that $EI$ has injective terms is required.
